extracted.intended_audience: US patent examiners, Central Reexamination Unit staff, and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination, interferences, and reissue matters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for processing, merging, suspending, and otherwise handling copending ex parte reexamination proceedings and their interaction with interferences and reissue applications. Covers notification duties, timelines, fees, and file-handling requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation Reminder (Patent Owner)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner is reminded of the continuing responsibility under 37 CFR 1.565(a), to apprise the Office of any litigation activity, or other prior or concurrent proceeding, involving Patent No. [1] throughout the course of this reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as form paragraph when granting an ex parte reexamination request filed by a patent owner and in first action in Director Ordered reexamination; see MPEP §§ 2207, 2282 and 2286.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation Reminder (Third Party Requester)
rubrics_metrics.description: The third party requester is reminded of the ability to similarly apprise the Office of any such activity or proceeding throughout the course of this reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph to be used when granting an ex parte reexamination request filed by a third party requester; see MPEP §§ 2207, 2282 and 2286.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question of Patentability for Subsequent Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for a second or subsequent request for ex parte reexamination to be granted, a substantial new question of patentability must be raised by the art (patents and/or printed publications) cited in the second or subsequent request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2240 for discussion on whether a substantial new question of patentability is raised by the prior art cited in a later request; second requests are decided on the claims in effect at time of determination (37 CFR 1.515(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger Generally Required but Discretionary
rubrics_metrics.description: If ex parte reexamination is ordered while a prior ex parte reexamination proceeding is pending and prosecution in the prior proceeding has not been terminated, the ex parte reexamination proceedings will usually be merged (37 CFR 1.565(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision to merge is within the sole discretion of the Office (CRU Director or delegate) and should facilitate the statutory mandate of special dispatch (35 U.S.C. 305). No decision on combining should be made until reexamination is actually ordered in the later-filed request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and Timely Processing of Multiple Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The second request should be processed as quickly as possible and assigned to the same examiner as Request 1. If neither request has been ordered, the examiner must address each request within three months of its filing date. If Request 1 has been ordered, Request 2 should be decided immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Request 2 is denied, ex parte prosecution of Request 1 should continue. If Request 2 is granted, the order in the second proceeding should be mailed immediately. Request 2 should be determined on its own merits and should not rely on or refer to the decision issued in Request 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and Conditions for Merger Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRU Director (or delegate) will prepare a decision whether to merge the two proceedings only after the patent owner's statement and any requester reply in Request 2 have been received or the time for filing has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision not to merge may be made where merging would unduly delay the first reexamination, contrary to 'special dispatch.' Merger decisions should indicate required actions (e.g., amendments) and be mailed immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Maintain Identical Claims in Merged Files
rubrics_metrics.description: A merger decision should include a requirement that the patent owner maintain identical claims in both files while proceedings remain merged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses and any paper filed in the merged proceeding must be a single response filed in duplicate, each bearing a signature and containing identifying data for both files. Files remain separate complete files even when proceedings are merged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housekeeping Amendment to Make Claims Identical
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claims are not the same in both files at time of merger, the decision will give the patent owner one month to provide an amendment to make the claims the same in each file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner must not address patentability in a housekeeping amendment. If the required identical-amendment is not timely submitted, any claim that does not contain identical text in all merged proceedings should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as indefinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of Single Combined Examiner Action for Merged Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution in merged proceedings is appropriate, a single combined examiner’s action will be prepared. Each action will contain control numbers of the proceedings on every page and a single action cover mailing sheet with both control numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support staff ensures action is processed and mailed to patent owner and each requester, that all parties receive copies and attachments, and that the entire action (mailing sheets and attachments) is scanned into the Image File Wrapper (IFW) database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution Continues at Most Advanced Point
rubrics_metrics.description: If proceedings are merged, prosecution will continue at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding. The examiner should prepare an Office action at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the first proceeding is ready for a final rejection and the second does not present new information calling for a new ground of rejection, the examiner should issue a final rejection for the merged proceeding using prosecution-stage guidelines. If new patents/publications in Request 2 create a new ground, prosecution may be reopened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of Proceedings—Extraordinary and Limited
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be desirable in certain situations to suspend a proceeding for a short and specified period (e.g., to allow time for the patent owner’s statement and requester’s reply in a second proceeding prior to merging).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension will only be granted in extraordinary instances because of statutory special dispatch; suspension will not be granted when there is an outstanding Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single Fee Rule in Merged Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed which requires payment of a fee (e.g., excess claim fee, extension of time request, petition fee, appeal fee, brief fee, oral hearing fee), only a single fee need be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although only one fee is paid, copies of the filing must be placed in each merged file as appropriate (e.g., one appeal brief fee covers multiple merged proceedings even though the brief relates to multiple merged proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to Merge are Generally Unnecessary and Premature Petitions Returned
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge multiple reexamination proceedings is necessary since the Office will generally sua sponte make a decision whether to merge. Any petition to merge filed prior to the determination (37 CFR 1.515) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) on the second request will not be considered and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent owner may file a petition to merge after the order to reexamine (best practice: include with patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530). Third party requesters lacking statutory standing cannot petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge with another reexamination where they lack standing; instead they may file a notification of concurrent proceedings under MPEP § 2282. Decisions on merits of petitions to merge are made by the CRU Director or delegate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and Identification Requirements for Contested Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In an appeal brief or at initiation of a contested case, and within 20 days of any change during the proceeding, a party must identify its real party-in-interest and each judicial or administrative proceeding that could affect, or be affected by, the Board proceeding (37 CFR 41.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contested cases, a party seeking judicial review must file a notice with the Board of the judicial review within 20 days of filing the complaint or notice of appeal, including a copy of the complaint or notice of appeal. See also §§ 1.301–1.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of Examination Before Contested Case
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a contested case is initiated, except as the Board may otherwise authorize, for each involved application and patent: (a) examination or reexamination must be completed, and (b) there must be at least one claim that (1) is patentable but for a judgment in the contested case, and (2) would be involved in the contested case (37 CFR 41.102).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures there is a concrete claim to be contested in the Board proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination Generally Not Delayed by Interference
rubrics_metrics.description: The general policy is that a reexamination proceeding will not be delayed, or stayed, because of an interference or the possibility of an interference, due to the requirement of 35 U.S.C. 305 that reexamination be conducted with 'special dispatch.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will generally make necessary decisions in the reexamination and go forward with the interference to the extent desirable; 37 CFR 41.103 gives the Board flexibility to tailor solutions. Note: a reexamination proceeding itself cannot be involved in an interference (only applications or patents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attempting to Provoke an Interference Against a Patent in Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is filed in a pending application seeking to provoke an interference with a patent involved in a reexamination proceeding, the applicant must comply with 37 CFR 41.202(a), including identifying the patent under reexamination with which interference is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding application claims may be rejected on any applicable ground including prior art cited in the reexamination. Examiner must notify OPLA before proposing interference; interference may not be proposed unless authorized by OPLA. If interference not authorized, suspend application prosecution until the reexamination certificate has issued and been published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion/Request to Suspend Interference Pending Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A miscellaneous motion under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(3) to suspend an interference pending the outcome of a reexamination proceeding may be made at any time during the interference by any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motion must be presented to the administrative patent judge who will decide based on the particular facts; suspension is not favored and normally not considered until a reexamination order is issued. If the APJ denies the motion, a request to stay the interference may be made to the Director under 37 CFR 1.565(e). A request to stay under 1.565(e) will be decided by the Chief Administrative Patent Judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination Requests Filed During an Interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file a request for reexamination at any time during the enforceability of a patent (37 CFR 1.510(a)). The patent owner must notify the Board that a request for reexamination was filed within 20 days of receiving notice of the request (37 CFR 41.8(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests will be processed normally; no delay or stay will occur merely because the requester is not a party to the interference. If an examiner orders reexamination and subsequently rejects a patent claim corresponding to a count in the interference, the Board shall be notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification When Interference Declared While Reexamination Ongoing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination patent becomes involved in an interference while reexamination is pending, the patent owner must file in the reexamination proceeding a paper giving notice of the interference proceeding (37 CFR 1.565 and 37 CFR 41.8(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements are designed to keep the Office and parties informed and to eliminate procedural surprise; upon issuance of a reexamination certificate, the patent owner must notify the administrative patent judge and the Board must be promptly notified of canceled or amended claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to Stay Reexamination Because of Interference—Timing and Proper Parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to stay a reexamination proceeding because of an interference filed prior to the determination (37 CFR 1.515) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.525) will not be considered and will be returned; a petition to stay may be filed by the patent owner as part of the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or subsequent thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party to the interference other than the patent owner is the requester of the reexamination, that party may petition to stay as part of a reply under 37 CFR 1.535. Petitions by parties who are not the requester are improper under 37 CFR 1.550(g) and will not be considered. Petitions filed after the order for reexamination are referred to OPLA; OPLA decides merits of petitions to stay due to interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Copending Reissue Application and Ex Parte Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reissue application and an ex parte reexamination on a patent are pending concurrently, a decision will usually be made to merge the two proceedings or to suspend one. Where merged, merged examination will be conducted in accordance with §§ 1.171–1.179, and the patent owner must place and maintain the same claims in the reissue application and the ex parte reexamination during the merged proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merged examiner actions and patent owner responses apply to both files and are physically entered into both. Any ex parte reexamination merged with a reissue application shall be concluded by the grant of the reissued patent. The decision whether to merge or stay is made by OPLA; notification of concurrent proceedings should be filed early (37 CFR 1.178(b), 1.565(a), 1.985).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Decision on Merging or Staying Reissue and Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision whether to merge the reissue application and reexamination or to stay one of the proceedings will not be made prior to the mailing of an order to reexamine pursuant to 37 CFR 1.525 and the expiration of the statement-reply period following the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination on the request must not be delayed because of a copending reissue application due to 35 U.S.C. 304 and 37 CFR 1.515 requiring determination within three months of the request filing. After reexamination order and statement-reply period, CRU SPRS or TC QAS should notify OPLA promptly that proceedings are ready for consideration of merger. If reissue patent issues prior to determination, reexamination should be based on reissue claims presented as a 'clean copy' (use form paragraph 22.05).
